blocks.text: Verified 55+ manufactured-home parks and co-ops: what the sources show

These are the 55+ places named in public sources where you can own the home. Pad rent, shares and fees quoted below are listing-stated for one home on one date, not a park tariff, so confirm them with the park. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
Alouette Retirement Mobile Home Park — 12868 229 St (East Central)

A 55+ manufactured home park in the residential streets east of downtown. A current listing states "55 PLUS age restriction — Alouette Retirement Mobile Home Park," with listing-stated terms: pad rental fee $713.31, city taxes $457.37, metered water billed quarterly, no dogs, indoor cat only, 2 residents per unit, and "no financing permitted in this community." All figures and rules are listing-stated — confirm against the park's tenancy agreement and park rules before relying on them. Park size (number of pads): UNCONFIRMED.
Val Maria — 21163 Lougheed Hwy (Southwest Maple Ridge)

A manufactured-home park on the Lougheed Highway corridor; current listing text for homes in the park states "VAL MARIA, 55+ age restricted manufactured home park," with a listing-stated monthly pad rent of $850 and 2 small pets allowed. The address carries multiple units in the topic feed. Listing-stated — confirm the age rule, pad rent and pet rules against the park's tenancy agreement and park rules. Park size (number of pads): UNCONFIRMED.

items.t: Manufactured-home parks run on tenancy law, not strata law: Pad tenancies are governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and its Regulation (B.C. Reg. 481/2003), not the Strata Property Act — so the strata age-bylaw machinery (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, Regulation 7.01 exemptions) does not apply inside a park. A home owner must provide a purchaser with the written tenancy agreement and the written park rules, and a sale is an assignment of the pad tenancy that requires the park owner's consent.

A park's 55+ rule has its own legal footing: The MHPTA assignment rules expressly recognise a park where every pad is reserved for a tenant who has reached 55 (or 2+ tenants, at least one of whom has reached 55), as set out in s. 10(2)(b)(i) of the Human Rights Code — the park owner can refuse an assignment where no purchaser meets that age requirement. That is how Alouette's and Val Maria's 55+ rules operate: through park rules and assignment consent, not through a strata bylaw.

For contrast — the strata rule that does NOT apply here: only 55+ age bylaws are legal in BC strata now (Strata Property Act, ss. 123.1 and 123.2; sub-55 bylaws invalid since Nov 24, 2022), and strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since the same date. A park can still set its own occupancy and rental rules in its park rules — do not import strata assumptions into a park purchase.
City zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, s. 626, Zone RMH (Manufactured Home Park Residential): is the dedicated zone for this housing form in Maple Ridge.
Tenure paperwork is the diligence core of a park purchase

The registry covers both manufactured and modular homes: The Province's manufactured-home registry covers both forms, which is why this page in practice covers manufactured and modular product together.

Floodplain: the City's floodplain framework (flood construction level 6.7 m geodetic including freeboard along the river flats; Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibiting rental accommodation/suites on floodplain properties) is per-lot diligence for any park or owned-land manufactured home at the city's south/west lowland edges.
Property taxes / deferment: Note the Alouette listing separately itemises "city taxes" on top of pad rent — who pays what on a pad is set by the tenancy agreement, not by strata practice.

blocks.text: Good to know before you buy a park home

items.t: The two 55+ entries in rest on current MLS listing text that names the park and states its age rule — solid enough to print as listing-stated, not a substitute for the park's own rules document.

The city's zoning has a park-specific zone. Zone RMH, Manufactured Home Park Residential (Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, s. 626) is a dedicated zone for this housing form — a park's zoning, not just its rules, is part of its long-term security.

The two verified parks sit at opposite ends of the core. Alouette (229 St) is in the East Central residential streets beside the Fraserview 55+ cluster; Val Maria (21163 Lougheed Hwy) is on the highway corridor in Southwest Maple Ridge — a "Maple Ridge 55+ park" search is really two different neighbourhood decisions.

"No financing permitted" is a park rule, not a lender decision. Alouette's listing states it outright — in park product, the park's own rules can close the financing question before any bank is asked.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge: how mobile and manufactured homes work here

items.t: This is a city-wide topic, not a neighbourhood: manufactured (mobile) homes for sale across the City of Maple Ridge — principally homes on rented pads in manufactured home parks, plus manufactured and modular homes on owned land.
Municipal zoning carries a dedicated zone for this housing form: Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 includes s. 626, Zone RMH, Manufactured Home Park Residential.
Schools: Maple Ridge is School District 42 (Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows).
A buyer reading "leasehold" on a listing there is looking at pad tenure, not a leasehold strata interest.
Ruskin Place's two age descriptions cannot both be used: A current secondary guide calls it family-friendly with no age restrictions; a 2015 classified called it "55+ Ruskin Park".

faq.q: What is the difference between a mobile home and a modular home in BC?
faq.a: Both are manufactured homes built off-site. The Province's registry distinguishes them by their CSA standard: mobile homes are built under the Z-240 standards and modular homes under the A-277 standards, and the CSA label on the home states which applies.

faq.q: Do I own the land under a Maple Ridge park home?
faq.a: In a manufactured home park, generally no: the Province describes park tenancies as owning the manufactured home and renting the site it sits on, under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act; the home's assessed value for tax purposes does not include the land value in a park.

faq.q: Can the park raise my pad rent when I buy?
faq.a: No — on assignment of the site tenancy the pad rental for the new tenant stays the same, and the scheduled date for a subsequent rent increase does not change; increases otherwise require 3 full months' notice, at most once every 12 months, within the yearly limit plus the proportional levy and utility amount.

faq.q: What if the home has lost its CSA label?
faq.a: A manufactured home may not be sold unless it has the original and legible CSA decal attached. If the label is removed or lost, the home must be re-certified: Technical Safety BC arranges a licensed electrical contractor's inspection, and the electrical approval label prepared can be used in place of a CSA label to list the home for sale.

faq.q: Which Maple Ridge parks are actually 55+?
faq.a: Two verify: Alouette Retirement Mobile Home Park (12868 229 St) and Val Maria (21163 Lougheed Hwy) — both on current listing text that names the park and states the 55+ age restriction. Any other Maple Ridge park claimed as 55+ is UNCONFIRMED in this research.

faq.q: What do I own when I buy in a 55+ park?
faq.a: The manufactured home — not the land. You rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, and your purchase is an assignment of that tenancy, which requires the park owner's consent.

faq.q: Can the park refuse me because of age — or refuse my buyer later?
faq.a: In a park whose pads are reserved by age, yes: the MHPTA assignment rules expressly recognise parks reserved for tenants who have reached 55 (Human Rights Code s. 10(2)(b)(i)), and the park owner can refuse an assignment where no purchaser meets the age requirement. The same rule that admits you at 55+ narrows your resale pool the same way a strata bylaw does.

faq.q: What are the carrying costs on top of the purchase?
faq.a: Pad rent is the big one, and it is park-specific: listing-stated figures are $713.31/month at Alouette (plus city taxes of $457.37 and quarterly metered water, per the same listing) and $850/month at Val Maria. Confirm the current figure for the specific pad in the tenancy agreement — pad rent is not a strata fee and is not set by the seller.

faq.q: Can I get a mortgage on a park home?
faq.a: It depends on the park — and at Alouette the listing states plainly "no financing permitted in this community." Read the park rules before assuming any lender product applies; a park purchase can be a cash purchase by rule, not just by price.

Park by park, and opposite at the two verified parks: Alouette's listing states no dogs, indoor cat only, 2 residents per unit; Val Maria's listing states 2 small pets allowed. Confirm in the park rules for the specific park.

Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street — a Fraser Health community hospital with 24/7 emergency care serving Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows. Both verified parks are in the urban core's orbit (229 Street east; Lougheed Highway west).

faq.q: Is a manufactured home on its own lot the same thing as a park home?
faq.a: No. A manufactured or modular home on owned land (the feed carried one on Calvin Crescent) is a freehold purchase — no pad rent, no park rules, no age restriction. The registry covers both forms, which is why they appear on the same page, but the tenure is entirely different.

faq.q: Do I own the land under a park home?
faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — a home on a rented pad is NOT land ownership. Own-land manufactured stock (fee-simple lot, bare-land strata lot, or a co-op share at The Maples) is a different purchase entirely.
Only as each park's own documents state it. The live topic page's broader "many parks are 55+" wording is site copy, not a verified park-by-park position. Get the specific park's written rules.

faq.q: Why does the CSA label matter?
faq.a: The sale is only effective once registered in the Manufactured Home Registry, and a home may not be sold unless its original legible CSA decal is attached (Z-240 mobile / A-277 modular); a lost label means Technical Safety BC re-certification before sale.
